items.title: Concord
items.note: A Sheffield dectet on Dwell Records playing five slow, improvised pieces with no drums and no voice. A Closer Listen says the players respond to tiny changes in each other's playing, and the shifts creep up on you over time.

items.title: One Of Many
items.note: The second album from an Amsterdam musician who composed, played and recorded all of it at home. It's self-released and tagged everywhere from Afro-Caribbean ritual music to drone and experimental jazz. That's exactly the kind of record an algorithm won't hand you.

items.title: Symbol Of The Land
items.note: Eleven tracks on the small Kynant label. Hard Wax calls it a warm, laid back, atmospheric dub electronic journey.

items.title: Toy (feat. Xenia Manasseh, tg.blk)
items.note: A soul single built around the back and forth between Xenia Manasseh and tg.blk. OkayAfrica calls it pure, unfiltered soul.

items.title: Bjerge, Strand
items.note: Bro's guitar with Larry Grenadier and Jorge Rossy, plus Charles Lloyd on saxophone and flute. JazzTrail calls it intimate and atmospheric, and picks out "Osaka" and "Peace Song" as favourites.

items.title: La Ola Nocturna: Experimental Songs and Deviant Pop from the Spanish 80's
items.note: Bongo Joe digs into post-punk, synthwave and darkwave from independent scenes across Spain after Franco, well beyond the usual Madrid Movida story. Bandcamp says it has something for both longtime fans and newcomers, with real oddities alongside the songs.

items.title: Wormhole Mystic
items.note: Minimal, rhythmic music built from synths, flute, saxophone and voice. It sits right where your beat and jazz sides meet.

items.title: Do Your Thing (A COLORS SHOW)
items.note: Her COLORS debut. OkayAfrica hears current British soul with a nostalgic swing, and it's a song about love.

items.title: Death/Rebirth One
items.note: Justin Broadrick's JK Flesh with the Canadian duo Orphx on KR3. Hard Wax sums it up as dark, heavy, raw techno, for when you want something with weight.

items.title: Forest of Tranquility
items.note: Seven long pieces on Erased Tapes in the Japanese environmental music tradition, each one shifting with the time of day. The press notes stress silence and point to Laraaji and Harold Budd. It's a quiet one to end on.
